title: Sign-in file (ship/signins/<id>.toml): how to sign a Ship in to a service, and how the Ship checks it
description: One file per sign-in flow; the file name must be <id>.toml. FleetLedger reads it to drive the login on the Ship (mode, run, match, after, logout, scopes) and to build its sign-in registry (signin, check); the Ship reads the same file, from its tooling bundle, for its status check (status). A file's status key is its id with '-' as '_' (gcloud-adc checks auth.gcloud_adc). The tables secret, params and levels are reserved for later login modes and are refused until then.

id.description: The flow's id (ship-fleet login SHIP <id>, ship-ctl notify-signin <id>); equal to the file name.

mode.description: paste-back: open the link, approve, paste the code shown back (match.prompt). device-code: the tool shows a code to type at the link (match.code).

run.description: The login command, run on the Ship as agent in a terminal.

timeout.description: Seconds the flow waits for the sign-in.

after.description: Commands run as agent once the login finished, before the checks.

match.description: Regular expressions over the login's terminal output.

send.description: Fixed answers: pattern = text typed once when it appears.

check.description: The status keys this flow signs in, in order, each with the command FleetLedger runs over SSH after a login on a Ship whose ship-ctl has no `signin check` (older tooling). Without it, the flow signs in its own status key only.

label.description: How the Sign-ins page names this status key (default: the sign-in's label).

short.description: How the fleet table names it (default: label).

signin.description: FleetLedger's sign-in registry: a sign-in people turn on or off per Ship (label, order), or a flow that signs in part of another one again (part_of). Without it the file is a flow only.

scopes.description: Extra scopes (GitHub): `add` is the flag run takes them with; `refresh` changes a signed-in token's scopes in place, with `add` and `remove` for the ones to add and drop.

status.description: How the Ship checks this file's status key, as agent, for `ship-ctl status` and `ship-ctl signin check`. Either a built-in check in ship-ctl (builtin), or a command (run) read as an adapter (exit code, ok_json, account, expires_at) or as the native status line (format = "shipshape": one line of JSON, {"shipshape_signin": 1, "state": ..., "account": ..., "expires_at": ..., "detail": ...}). A command check has 5 seconds; its result is kept for `every` between status refreshes; a check that times out shows unknown.

run.description: Run with bash -c as agent, stdin empty. Only stdout is read (at most 64 KiB), and dropped once parsed.

every.description: How long a result is kept before the check runs again (default 5m; 0s: every refresh). `ship-ctl signin check` always runs it.

format.description: adapter (default): exit code, ok_json, account, expires_at. shipshape: the native status line.

ok_json.description: stdout is JSON; signed in when the value at this path is true (or any non-empty value).

account.description: The account: stdout (its first non-empty line), json:<path>, or re:<regular expression with one group> over stdout.

expires_at.description: When the sign-in ends, as RFC 3339 or epoch seconds: json:<path> or re:<one group>. Report the sign-in's end, never a short-lived access token's (a tool renews those by itself).

expiring_within.description: Signed in, but ending within this: state expiring (default 24h).

missing_exit.description: Exit codes that mean not signed in (missing); any other non-zero exit is error. Default: every non-zero exit is missing.

discard_output.description: true for a check whose output may hold a token: stdout and stderr go to /dev/null and only the exit code counts.

secrets.description: Where the tool keeps this sign-in on the Ship: documentation and checks only, never values.

paths.description: Files or folders under the agent's home that hold the sign-in.

store.description: Where the tool stores it: its own files. A password store (keyring) is refused: a Ship has no unlocked one, so pin the tool to its file store.

allOf.description: A sign-in of its own is named by its id in ships.toml (signins, [tag.*]): no '-'.

statusLabel.description: How the Ship's attention items and notices name the status key (default: the file's label).
